requirements.title: Lower-division courses (9 credits)

rule.manualCheck: AAS 211 and AAS 212 count only for the appropriate topic. Courses listed with '/' are alternatives (e.g., AAS 250 / LIN 250); count only one course from each such pair. requirements.title: Upper Division Courses (9 credits)

rule.manualCheck: AAS 340 / HIS 340 (Topics in Asian History), ANT 311, HIS 300, and LIN 431 count only for the appropriate topic. Courses listed with '/' are alternatives (e.g., AAS 380 / RLS 380; AAS 472 / PHI 472); count only one course from each such pair. AAS 447 carries 1-6 credits and AAS 487 carries 0-3 credits, so credit totals must be verified. Courses not listed may be counted at the discretion of the director of the minor, if they have a substantial component relating to South Asian Studies; this cannot be checked automatically.

notes.text: The minor consists of six courses (18 credits): three lower-division (nine credits) and three upper-division (nine credits). With the approval of the director of the minor, the student constructs a coherent and individualized program of study.

Other minors of particular interest to students minoring in South Asian Studies: Anthropology (ANT), China Studies (CNS), International Studies (INT), Japanese Studies (JNH), Korean Studies (KOR), Religious Studies (RLS).

The Center for India Studies (telephone: 631-632-9742), located in E-5350 Melville Library, offers a reference library, lectures and performing arts programs, publications, and internship opportunities for students minoring in South Asian Studies. Visit http://www.sunysb.edu/india for details.
Students may also earn academic credits through Study Abroad in India opportunities.
